Issue reference: https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/38513

`task_filter()` would filter out tasks when manually triggering tasks with a future `start_date`, causing them to not run while the dag would be marked as a success. Created a condition to bypass the filter if `run_type` is MANUAL

issue_context.title: DAGs with future `start_date` are automatically marked as success without executing tasks
issue_context.body:
### Body

For the following DAG:

```
from datetime import datetime

from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator

default_args = {
    'owner': 'airflow',
}

with DAG('my_future_dag',
         default_args=default_args,
         start_date=datetime(2050, 1, 1),
         schedule="@daily",
         catchup=False
         ):
    BashOperator(task_id="task1", bash_command="echo 1")
    BashOperator(task_id="task2", bash_command="echo 2")
    BashOperator(task_id="task3", bash_command="echo 3")
    BashOperator(task_id="task4", bash_command="echo 4")
```

 
As expected no runs will be started till 2050 but I might still want to manually invoke runs. Trying to do so will result in DAGRun marked as success and no tasks being executed as can see 
 
 
![Screenshot 2024-03-26 at 22 22 42](https://github.com/apache/airflow/assets/45845474/93c2cee0-e3a4-41c4-bc0f-0fbd3bc9da38)

However changing the `start_date` to `datetime(2023, 1, 1)` then tasks are executed as expected for manual runs:
![Screenshot 2024-03-26 at 22 24 28](https://github.com/apache/airflow/assets/45845474/32369453-2036-4e92-ab77-a7ee9ec1b260)


**The bug:**
tasks should be executed for manual runs. The current case where dagrun is marked as success but no tasks are running or reporting failure is wrong.


By the way, a very interesting thing to explore is that if you first deploy the dag with `datetime(2023, 1, 1)` then change it to `datetime(2050, 1, 1)` Airflow has no problem with running tasks with that `start_date`:

![Screenshot 2024-03-26 at 22 28 19](https://github.com/apache/airflow/assets/45845474/7abca52a-3bed-49e4-89fd-6fef8213e747)


![Screenshot 2024-03-26 at 22 29 36](https://github.com/apache/airflow/assets/45845474/832706bd-af4f-418e-b9c6-14c83187ce9b)






### Committer

- [X] I acknowledge that I am a maintainer/committer of the Apache Airflow project.
comments:
https://forum.astronomer.io/t/dag-run-marked-as-success-but-no-tasks-even-started/1423
https://stackoverflow.com/q/73652663

We usually have users using dynamic start_date which causes the issue. We point them to these links. It will be helpful if these dagruns are blocked from marked as success.
Dynamic start date is wrong usage. The case that I show here is valid.
@eladkal I want to try my hand at this one, seems interesting. Can I take it up?
@amoghrajesh have you been able to figure out what is causing this?

regarding the note about the tasks running if you deploy the dag with a past start_date and change it to a future start_date, it will run the tasks properly for a while but then revert to the old behaviour after manually triggering the dag a few times

side note: same issue behaviour when manual run is triggered after end_date

This is the same for manually-triggered DAG runs with a logical date that is before the `start_date`. I would expect/hope that manually triggered runs with a logical date prior to the `start_date` of the DAG would actually run. However, they do not (i.e.,  none of the tasks run; instead, the DAG run is just marked as an immediate success).

I have a use case for this where I have a DAG that schedules a compute-intensive Spark job on an EMR cluster. Because of the nature of the upstream dataset (there is late-arriving data), the Spark job processes data with a 7-day lookback window from each `data_interval_start`. The job runs twice daily. As a result, some of the same data is reprocessed. I set the start date to `2024-12-01`. But I would like to backfill data from `2024-10-01` to `2024-12-01`.

I don't want to set the `start_date` to `2024-10-01` with `catchup=True` because the late-arriving data has already arrived for the historical months. In other words, I don't want to have ≈120 DAG runs get scheduled for the preceding two months. Instead, I'd like to just run some manual DAG runs: `2024-10-07`, `2024-10-14`, `2024-10-21`, `2024-10-28`, _etc._. Since the late-arriving data has already arrived for these historical months, I don't want to have several overlapping runs with a sliding lookback window. Instead, I just want to trigger several manual runs each of which is spaced 7 days apart for the historical months.

I see that @artilexx had done some initial work to address this in #40711 but it was closed due to inactivity.

Is there still interest in merging this? If so, happy to take a shot at it when I can find time and also try to make it work for my use case with manually-triggered DAG runs with a logical date prior to the `start_date`. (But also don't want to step on @artilexx's toes if they want to pick it back up.)
@adamliter feel free to pick it up. The changes I made definitely fixed the problem with DAGs not running when I tested it out, but it also broke the UI (iirc) and I was never able to figure out why.
